title: 长寿干预的证据分级:雷帕霉素、二甲双胍、NAD+、禁食(深入版) — BigCat Deep Research
title_en: Grading the Evidence on Longevity Interventions: Rapamycin, Metformin, NAD+, Fasting (Deep Dive) — BigCat Deep Research

questions.question: 常被引用的「雷帕霉素延长小鼠寿命 14%」，按长寿证据综述的拆解，问题出在哪里？
options: 这个数字是伪造的，雷帕霉素在小鼠身上并不能延长寿命
它是 90% 死亡年龄口径、600 日龄才开始给药，不是中位寿命增幅
它确实是中位寿命增幅，问题只在于实验只用了单一近交系小鼠
它来自人体临床试验，但被误当成小鼠数据引用
questions.explanation: 雷帕霉素在动物层的证据是四个干预里最强的，问题不在真假，而在口径：原文的 14% 是 90% 死亡年龄的增幅，起始时间已是暮年，引用时被当成中位寿命。综述强调这类滑坡不是造假，而是把一个数字从它成立的口径搬到不成立的口径；ITP 用的恰恰是四向杂种而非近交系。
questions.question_en: A widely cited claim says rapamycin extends mouse lifespan by 14%. According to the longevity-evidence review, what is wrong with how this figure is used?
options_en: The number is fabricated; rapamycin doesn't actually extend mouse lifespan
It measures age at 90% mortality—a maximum-lifespan metric—with dosing started at 600 days, not a median lifespan gain; it's an endpoint slip
It really is a median lifespan gain; the only problem is that the study used a single inbred mouse strain
It comes from a human clinical trial but is misquoted as mouse data
questions.explanation_en: Rapamycin has the strongest animal evidence of the four interventions; the issue isn't truth but framing. The original 14% is the gain in age at 90% mortality, with treatment starting in old age, yet it gets quoted as a median lifespan gain. The review stresses that such slips aren't fraud—they move a number from the frame where it holds to one where it doesn't. And the ITP mice are four-way crosses, not an inbred strain.

questions.question: 英国一项研究曾报告「服用二甲双胍的糖尿病人比匹配的健康人活得更久」。后来威尔士 SAIL 数据库的分析对此最有价值的贡献是什么？
options: 证实了原结论，二甲双胍组在二十年随访中仍比健康对照活得更久
发现原研究的数据是伪造的，因此被撤稿
发现二甲双胍组和健康对照在任何时间窗口下都没有差别
发现二甲双胍组的生存优势在头三年存在、五年后反转，从而解释了原结论是短随访造成的假象
questions.explanation: 原结论来自中位随访约 2.4 年的模型外推，粗死亡率差异本身也不显著；丹麦数据给出相反方向。威尔士数据二十年口径下二甲双胍组生存时间只有对照的 82%，更关键的是在模拟研究窗口中重现了「头三年有优势、五年后反转」，对假象给出了机制解释。原论文至今也没有撤稿。
questions.question_en: A UK study once reported that diabetics taking metformin lived longer than matched non-diabetic controls. What was the most valuable contribution of the later analysis of Wales's SAIL database?
options_en: It confirmed the original finding: the metformin group still outlived healthy controls over twenty years
It found the original study's data were fabricated, leading to a retraction
It found no difference between the metformin group and healthy controls in any time window
It found metformin's survival advantage exists for the first three years and reverses after five, explaining the original result as an artifact of short follow-up
questions.explanation_en: The original claim was a model-based extrapolation from a median follow-up of about 2.4 years, and its crude mortality difference wasn't even significant; Danish data pointed the other way. Over twenty years, the Welsh metformin group's survival time was only 82% of controls'—but the key contribution was reproducing an advantage in the first three years that reverses after five across simulated study windows, giving a mechanism for the artifact. The original paper has not been retracted.

questions.question: NIA 干预测试计划（ITP）在一轮新实验中，几个此前报告过约 8–12% 小幅延寿的化合物都没有再显著。按综述的判断，应如何解读？
options: 重测改了剂量或起始年龄且功效不足，不算复现失败；小效应命中本就脆弱
说明效应确实存在，这次不显著只是因为对照组鼠寿命太短
说明连金标准程序也复现不了自己的结果，所以 ITP 过去的所有结论都不可信
说明这些化合物此前的结果都是造假
questions.explanation: 综述撤回了「金标准复现不了自己」的写法：改了条件的阴性结果是另一个实验，而功效不足时「不显著」不等于「不存在」。ITP 的大效应命中（雷帕霉素、阿卡波糖、17α-雌二醇）复现得很稳，脆弱的是低于约 10% 检出下限的小命中，ITP 自己也承认它们可能是偶然。
questions.question_en: In a new round of the NIA Interventions Testing Program (ITP), several compounds that had previously shown small lifespan gains of roughly 8–12% were no longer significant. How does the review say this should be read?
options_en: The retests changed dose or starting age and lacked power to detect the original effects, so they aren't replication failures; small hits sit at the power floor and are inherently fragile
It shows the effects are real, and this round failed only because the control mice died unusually early
It shows even the gold-standard program can't replicate itself, so none of the ITP's conclusions can be trusted
It shows the earlier results for these compounds were fabricated
questions.explanation_en: The review retracts the line 'the gold standard can't replicate itself': a negative result under changed conditions is a different experiment, and with insufficient power, 'not significant' doesn't mean 'absent.' The ITP's large hits—rapamycin, acarbose, 17α-estradiol—replicate robustly; what's fragile are small hits below the roughly 10% detection floor, which the ITP itself concedes may be chance.
